In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loadability of distribution systems can be increased by PV units, but this is not true for all systems.
the static voltage stability of a distribution system is improved with the increase in PV penetration.
the PV units can improve the static voltage stability of a distribution system, but this improvement would depend on the location of PV units, their power rating and the load parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PV can improve the loadability of distribution system in the range of 0.2 to 0.4 per unit of real power injection.
, the loadability of distribution system can be improved with the help of real power injection from PV and the improvement is more significant for the systems with high line and load impedences.
the static voltage stability of a distribution system can be improved by injecting real power from PV, while the reactive power injection can worsen the static voltage stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the loadability of an actual distribution system can be estimated by using simple two-bus equivalent networks and the results can be used for assessing the possibility of improvement of loadability by PV injection.
PV injection can improve the loadability of distribution system by reducing the voltage drop.
PV can be used as an effective means to increase the loadability of power system.
